name: Operating Company Growth Equity
summary: Covers minority or control growth equity into small and mid-size private operating companies: the catch-all for inbound raises that are neither early-stage venture nor leveraged buyouts, including founder- and family-owned businesses taking their first institutional capital. Growth equity carries little leverage, so the return must come from revenue growth and the exit multiple. The spine: underwrite flat margins, a forecast haircut of about 20% and an exit at or below entry; test management's forecast record against the last three budgets; rebuild revenue from cash and cohorts; and, as a minority holder, diligence the preference stack and who can block or reprice the next round. Sector metrics come from the relevant chapter (SaaS in tech-venture, CPG in cpg-consumer).
one_check: Re-run the return with flat margins, a 20% forecast haircut and exit at the entry multiple; if it no longer clears the hurdle (22% to 25% gross IRR, about 2.5x MOIC), the deal is a bet on the multiple.

subtypes.name: Minority growth equity
subtypes.description: Non-control investment alongside founders or existing investors. Preference stack and control map, every veto and its holder, insider-round history, information and time rights, strategic investors on the cap table.

subtypes.name: Control growth equity
subtypes.description: Majority growth investment with little or no leverage. Same return discipline, plus governance rebuild (independent board, real CFO) and management incentives.

subtypes.name: Family- or founder-owned first institutional round
subtypes.description: Owner-run companies raising outside capital for the first time. Governance pre-conditions (independent board with an audit-capable director, a real CFO, next generation with outside experience before board seats), related-party clean-up, sloppy-numbers signal.

intake_questions.question: Are we taking a minority or control position, and is the company founder- or family-owned with no prior institutional capital?
What is the sector, and which sector chapter's metrics apply (SaaS, CPG, other)?
intake_questions.why: Growth equity borrows sector metrics; always add runway, burn, growth, gross margin and retention.

intake_questions.question: What are the use of proceeds and the path to the next round or to profitability?
intake_questions.why: Runway must reach the next round at today's cadence (at least 24 months).

intake_questions.question: Who else is on the cap table, including strategic or corporate investors, and who holds vetoes over financing or M&A?
intake_questions.why: Triggers preference-stack and control map (Zync, Footprint).

intake_questions.question: Have there been prior bridge or down rounds, and are insiders participating in this round?
Is the company in a hot theme (AI, climate, space, crypto)?
intake_questions.why: Triggers theme-timing comparison of entry valuation.

intake_questions.question: Is there a CFO, and who on the board could chair an audit committee?

requests.request: Provide historical financial statements (3 years plus TTM) and monthly management accounts.
requests.format: Audited, reviewed or compiled statements; monthly packs.
requests.why: Sloppy numbers signal broader governance problems.
requests.pass: Monthly accounts consistent with annual statements; no restatements between versions.
requests.verify: Tie to tax returns and bank statements.

requests.request: Provide the last three years of budgets with actuals.
requests.pass: Misses not consistently optimistic; variances explained.

requests.request: Provide management's forecast with its downside case.
requests.why: Management ranges too narrow (36% hit rate).
requests.pass: Downside provided so we can treat it as a midpoint and widen ranges.

requests.request: Provide the fully diluted cap table with every instrument and the preference stack.
requests.pass: Every instrument listed and tied to a signed document; preference stack modeled.

requests.request: Provide the customer-cohort file: customers acquired, active customers and orders per period.
requests.pass: Complete file reconciling to revenue within 2%.
requests.fail: Cannot or will not produce it.

requests.request: Provide use of proceeds and the path to the next round or profitability with runway.
requests.why: Running out of runway at today's cadence.
requests.pass: Runway at least 24 months to the next round, or a funded path to profitability.

requests.request: Provide the treasury map: balances by bank, insured share and any single-bank covenant.
requests.why: Cash stranded at a failed bank.
requests.pass: No more than a quarter of payroll uninsured at one bank; no single-bank covenant without sweeps.

requests.request: Provide the valuation rationale and comparables, with the dates of the theme's media and fund-launch peak if in a hot theme.
requests.why: Buying a theme at its peak.
requests.pass: Entry valuation consistent with sector history.

requests.request: Provide management bios and at least 8 to 10 references, including former colleagues we may choose.
requests.pass: References completed, including ones we source.

requests.request: Provide a base case with EBITDA margin flat at current, management's forecast haircut about 20%, and exit at or below entry.
requests.pass: Base case clears 22% to 25% gross IRR and about 2.5x MOIC.

requests.request: Provide the 2x test: the exit multiple at which the deal returns 2x on flat margins and haircut revenue.
requests.pass: 2x exit multiple at or below entry.

requests.request: Provide the return attribution: revenue growth, margin change and multiple change, and the share surviving flat margins and exit at entry.
requests.why: Growth case that looks like multiple expansion (80% in search-fund data).
requests.pass: Majority of return from revenue growth; surviving share reported.

requests.request: Provide a line-by-line cost bridge for any margin expansion, naming each cost line and its evidence.
requests.why: Margin expansion with no named cost line.
requests.pass: Each line supported; otherwise base case flat.

requests.request: Provide the control map: every veto over financing, debt and M&A, who holds it, and who can lead or block the next round.
requests.pass: No strategic holds a financing veto, or it is waived or priced.

requests.request: Provide the history of every prior bridge and down round: price, participants, insiders' marks and time given to non-participants.
requests.pass: Prior rounds priced at or above insiders' marks with alternatives documented.
requests.fail: Insider rounds below marks with short windows.

requests.request: Provide the rights of every strategic or corporate investor on the cap table.
requests.why: Technology leakage, exit blocking and no follow-on.
requests.pass: No ROFR on company sale; information rights ring-fenced; no reliance on CVC follow-on.
requests.fail: ROFR on sale or financing veto.

requests.request: Provide the proposed preference, information, board and time rights for our security, including rights in any future insider round.
requests.why: Minority holders squeezed in future rounds.
requests.pass: Pre-emptive rights, information rights, board or observer seat, and minimum notice period for future rounds.
requests.fail: No protection in future insider rounds.

requests.request: Commit to governance pre-conditions before funding: an independent board with at least one director able to chair audit, a real CFO, and a board reconfigured for a downturn.
requests.format: Board plan and CFO hire plan.
requests.pass: Pre-conditions met at or before closing.

requests.request: Provide the policy for next-generation family members joining the board.
requests.why: Unprepared next generation on the board.
requests.pass: Next generation has worked outside the business (practitioners suggest 7 to 10 years and a C-level role) before a board seat.

requests.request: Provide QoE-lite data: revenue by customer and product, margin build, working capital monthly, and revenue reconciled to bank deposits.
requests.pass: Revenue reconciles to cash within 2% monthly; margins tie to GL.

requests.request: Provide unit economics by product or segment.
requests.pass: Positive contribution in growth segments.

requests.request: Provide top-10 customer revenue by period for the customer-side revenue test, with authorization to confirm.
requests.why: Revenue fraud visible in customer data.
requests.pass: Sales move with customers' purchases; no jumps in customer inventory or payables.

requests.request: Provide customer concentration, pipeline and competitive landscape.
requests.pass: Concentration priced; pipeline conversion supported by history.

requests.request: Provide access to a random sample of customers for live-activity or reference testing.
requests.pass: Sampled customers active and confirm relationship.
requests.verify: Our engineer or analyst draws the sample.

requests.request: Provide cohort revenue curves and share of revenue from newly acquired customers.
requests.pass: New cohorts at least as valuable as prior; share of new-customer revenue stable.

requests.request: Provide NRR and GRR from the raw customer-level file.
requests.pass: Benchmarked against private median NRR just above 100% and GRR near 90%.

requests.request: Provide a schedule of related-party revenue, expenses and balances.
requests.pass: All disclosed and at arm's length or normalized.
requests.fail: Undisclosed items found in bank review.

requests.request: Provide charter, prior financing documents, IP assignments, material contracts and litigation schedule.
requests.pass: Complete and consistent with cap table.

requests.request: Provide the CFO's background and the finance team structure.
requests.why: A controller with a CFO title.
requests.pass: CFO with audited-company or institutional experience.

requests.request: Provide the board roster with skills, independence and audit-committee capability.
requests.why: No director able to chair audit.
requests.pass: At least one independent director able to chair audit.

requests.request: Provide a key-person risk assessment and succession plan.
requests.pass: Named successors.

requests.request: Record in-person management hours, sites visited and references called by our team and the lead investor.
requests.pass: Diligence floor met regardless of competition.

requests.request: Provide access for the QoE-lite engagement.
requests.pass: No unreconciled items.

requests.request: Sign consents for background checks on management.
requests.pass: No adverse findings.

requests.request: Provide counsel access for the legal diligence review.
requests.pass: No material issues.

requests.request: Deliver the reconciled closing cap table and executed documents.
requests.pass: Zero exceptions.

requests.request: Deliver evidence that governance pre-conditions are in place (independent director, CFO, audit committee).
requests.pass: In place at closing.

requests.request: Deliver waivers or amendments for any strategic financing veto.
requests.pass: No strategic financing veto survives.

requests.request: Deliver treasury diversification at funding.
requests.pass: Treasury test passes.

requests.request: Deliver monthly accounts and quarterly budget-vs-actual.
requests.pass: Misses explained.

requests.request: Deliver quarterly cohort and retention data.
requests.pass: Stable or improving cohorts.

requests.request: Notify us of any new financing proposal, insider round or veto exercise with time and information to respond.
requests.pass: Notice at least as long as agreed with full information.

requests.request: Deliver quarterly runway and treasury map.
requests.pass: Runway at least 24 months or funded plan.

kill_tests.test: Return fails the hurdle with flat margins, a 20% forecast haircut and exit at the entry multiple, and the case relies on multiple expansion.
No clean cap table; unpapered instruments that cannot be reconciled before signing.
Revenue cannot be reconciled to cash.
Founder will not provide references or raw data.
Company cannot produce customers acquired and active customers by period.
Family or founder company refuses the governance pre-conditions (independent audit-capable director, real CFO) before investment.

red_flags.flag: No clean cap table; unpapered instruments.
red_flags.check: Reconcile every instrument to signed documents.
Bank deposits to revenue by month.

red_flags.flag: Founder will not provide references or raw data.

red_flags.check: Related-party schedule; bank-statement review for related-party flows.

red_flags.flag: A history of budgets missed optimistically.
A 'CFO' who is really a controller; no director able to chair audit.
red_flags.check: Interview the CFO; board skills map.

red_flags.flag: Margin expansion in the plan with no named cost line.
red_flags.check: Flat-margin base case; line-by-line cost bridge for any expansion.

red_flags.flag: Exit case that needs a multiple above entry.
Insiders leading a round priced below their own recent marks, with a short window for others.
red_flags.check: Price against insiders' marks; information and time rights for non-participants.

red_flags.flag: A strategic investor with a veto over financing.
red_flags.check: List every veto and holder; require waiver or price it.

red_flags.flag: Raised into a theme at its media peak.
red_flags.check: Compare entry valuation with sector history and theme media peak.
Request customers acquired, active and orders by period.

red_flags.flag: Next generation taking board seats without outside experience.
red_flags.check: Require 7 to 10 years outside and a C-level role (practitioner suggestion) before a board seat.

red_flags.flag: Sloppy or inconsistent numbers even where unaudited.
red_flags.check: Treat as a broader governance signal; expand financial diligence.

red_flags.flag: Diligence hours shrinking because the round is competitive.
red_flags.check: Record in-person hours, sites and references; hold the floor.

red_flags.flag: Reliance on a corporate VC for follow-on capital.
red_flags.check: Assume no CVC follow-on (median CVC life four years).

metrics.acceptable: About 20% off management EBITDA (median and mean).
About 75% of PE survey respondents invest in growth equity; same benchmarks apply.
Flat at current EBITDA margin in base case; no average expansion across 6,103 high-growth firms. CONTRADICTS implicit expansion in most growth models; expansion only with a named, costed driver.
metrics.source: Thomas, Ertan and Lewellen, Yale Insights

metrics.acceptable: Solve for the exit multiple returning 2x on flat margins and haircut revenue; compare with entry. It should be at or below entry.
At least 24 months to the next round (616 days median seed to A, Q2 2025).
Just above 100% (NDR 101% in 2024); not the 117% top-quartile figure. Sources conflict (v1 vendor figure about 117%, WEAK): benchmark the median on KeyBanc/Sapphire.
Outcomes inside CFOs' 80% intervals only 36% of the time: treat management's downside as a midpoint.
About a quarter of AAER misstatements began as optimistic errors.
Not reliably better (Moskowitz and Vissing-Jorgensen 2002; disputed beyond 1990s by Kartashova 2011): do not assume an illiquidity premium.
metrics.source: NBER w8876; Bank of Canada WP 2011-6

metrics.acceptable: About 80% of value creation from multiple expansion; margins fell (25% to 19%): a growth case that looks the same is a warning.
metrics.source: Wasserstein and Thomas, Yale Insights, Apr. 2026

metrics.acceptable: Median four years; do not count on follow-on.
Practitioners suggest 7 to 10 years outside the business and a C-level role before a board seat.
metrics.source: O'Dowd and McLarty, Yale Insights (practitioner suggestion)

metrics.acceptable: Default-alive runway, burn, growth, gross margin, retention: use sector benchmarks from tech-venture or cpg-consumer.

third_party_reports.report: QoE-lite (revenue quality, margins, working capital, revenue to cash)
Background checks and references on management
third_party_reports.provider: Background-check provider; our own reference calls

third_party_reports.report: Legal diligence on cap table, charter, prior financings, IP, material contracts and litigation

third_party_reports.provider: Commercial diligence firm or deal team

third_party_reports.report: Customer-side revenue confirmation for top 10 customers

hard_questions.question: Show the last three budgets against actuals.
hard_questions.good_answer: Budgets and actuals for three years with misses not consistently optimistic and explained.

hard_questions.question: Which cost lines fall as a share of revenue in the plan, and what evidence supports each?
hard_questions.good_answer: A line-by-line bridge with contracts or quotes, or a flat-margin plan.

hard_questions.question: At flat margins and a 20% revenue haircut, what exit multiple returns 2x?
hard_questions.good_answer: A multiple at or below entry.

hard_questions.question: Who can block or lead the next round, and what happened in every prior bridge or down round?
hard_questions.good_answer: A complete rights map and a history of prior rounds priced fairly with alternatives documented.

hard_questions.question: Who on the cap table is a strategic, and what rights do they hold?
hard_questions.good_answer: A list of strategics with no financing veto and no ROFR on a sale.

hard_questions.question: Is your CFO a CFO? Who on the board can chair audit?
hard_questions.good_answer: A CFO with audited-company experience and an independent director qualified to chair audit.

hard_questions.question: How many weeks of payroll survive if your main bank closes?
hard_questions.good_answer: At least a quarter's payroll diversified across banks or in insured or Treasury balances.

hard_questions.question: How many customers did you acquire and keep, by period?
hard_questions.good_answer: Acquired and active counts by period from the production system, reconciled to revenue.

hard_questions.question: How much of the return survives flat margins and exit at entry?
hard_questions.good_answer: A stated share of the sponsor-case return that still clears the hurdle.

hard_questions.question: What is the use of proceeds, and does it reach the next round or profitability?
hard_questions.good_answer: A milestone budget with runway of at least 24 months.

failure_cases.what_happened: $450M of a $500M round from three insider funds at about half their own implied value; three weeks to decide.
failure_cases.check: Preference-stack and control map; price against insiders' marks; information and time rights for non-participants.

failure_cases.what_happened: Strategic's designee voted down a $10M Series A; company shut down.

failure_cases.case: Forecast optimism becomes misreporting (Schrand and Zechman)
failure_cases.what_happened: About a quarter of AAER misstatements began as optimistic errors.

failure_cases.case: Margin plan never arrives (Thomas, Ertan and Lewellen)
failure_cases.what_happened: No average margin expansion with growth across 6,103 IPO firms.
Growth bought with marketing; collapsing or acquisition-only cohorts.
Cash stranded at a failed bank.

failure_cases.check: Governance map; real CFO; audit-capable director.
